To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

The likelihood ratio statistic is generally more powerful than the ANOVA F-statistic for testing the null value of the variance component in a model with a random effects term, and is rarely less powerful.

(a) the F-statistic is usually more powerful than the likelihood ratio statistic when testing for non-zero values of the between- group variance component, and (b) the likelihood ratio statistic may be more powerful than the test statistic in the case where the data is extremely unbalanced and the null hypothesis is that the between-group variance is zero.
The likelihood ratio statistic can sometimes be more powerful than the standard F-statistic in a random effects model for testing non-zero values.
